svg.title: Thicken (Solidify) modifier: how a surface gets thickness
svg.desc: The surface is copied and moved against its normals by the thickness (a share of the object size), turned inside out, and joined to the original along every open edge with a wall that has its own points. Corners are pushed further so the wall is evenly thick. A plane becomes a slab, an open shape a shell, a closed shape a hollow.
svg.text: Thicken (Solidify) modifier (Phase 13, step 4a)
A normal modifier: non-destructive, reorderable, can be switched off, and Make mesh bakes it in.
1. The surface
normals (the way it faces)
points on one spot count as one
2. A copy, pushed back
thickness
turned inside out (winding flipped)
3. Walls on open edges
a wall joins the two copies
with its own points: a crisp edge
What you get
plane: a closed slab, volume = area x thickness (tested exactly)
open shape (bowl, leaf, cloth): a shell with a rim
closed shape (cube): hollow inside, no walls needed; the wall is evenly thick (cube: volume 1 - 0.8 cubed)
Thickness is a share of the object size (-0.5 to 0.5, default 0.1). Negative grows the other way. Reset button on the slider.
Nothing happens for 0 thickness, an empty mesh, or when the result would pass the point limit.
Even thickness
A corner point is pushed along the average of its faces' normals (each face weighted by the angle it fills there, so the way a
square is split into triangles does not matter), and the push is longer by 1 / cos of the angle (at most 2x). Without it the
walls of a hollowed cube would be thinner at the corners.
Code: packages/shared/src/solidify.ts, the modifier list in modifiers.ts, one slider in ModifiersSection.tsx
